principles.text: Validate first: put up a landing page, message practitioners, and show a cheap mockup to 10-20 people before building.
Find repetitive tasks companies already pay people to do, and automate them with AI.
Drop the free plan and raise prices; B2B customers who fit will pay the extra buck.
Spend time on work that brings revenue and reaches your target audience, not on your next post.
Early on, prioritize growth over profitability and pay others for what you can outsource.

sampleQA.question: Should I keep a free plan or free trial on my B2B SaaS?

answer.text: He removed Affistash's free trial: it converted badly, burned bandwidth, and drew low-quality signups making multiple accounts to farm credits.
Six weeks after removing the free plan, churn was down 54%, revenue up 64% and subscriber LTV up 218%.
He also raised prices; $97/mo became his best price point, with customers calling it a no-brainer for the ROI.

sampleQA.question: How do I validate a SaaS idea before building it?

answer.text: Put up a quick landing page with an email collection section before you build.
Message practitioners in subreddits, communities and LinkedIn, have them walk through their process, and look for the manual steps.
Show a Canva or Figma mockup to 10-20 people, and weight experts' opinions far above friends and family.

sampleQA.question: How do I sell a small SaaS?

answer.text: Tweet it: one semi-viral post brought 10-15 interested buyers in DMs and a quick sale to a CTO.
He listed Coverposts on Twitter with users, churn, LTV and a sub-$4k price, and sold it in 2 days without marketplaces.
Marketplaces like Microns and TinyAcquisitions also work; his first micro SaaS drew two offers at $3.7k.
Don't sell just because motivation dips: he turned down Affistash offers and called not exiting his best decision.
